example_input: Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.narrative: The prompt arrives in the Web UI — the primary surface, a React client served by a node:http plugin on 127.0.0.1:3080; there is no interactive TUI. Before the loop touches it, the message is appended to the session's append-only event log. The session itself was created under the Standard preset with its permission pair (workspace-write sandbox, ask approvals) already pinned into the log as a permission/preset event — later settings changes never rewrite an existing session.
steps.representation:
session log (append-only, format v4)
  ...
  permission/preset   { sandbox: workspace-write, approval: ask }
  user/message        "Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page"
# nothing is model-visible unless it is in this log
steps.title: The prompt is logged first

steps.narrative: Each step of the loop starts by pricing the pending request through ctx.tokenMeter. The compaction plugin (mounted in the base bundle, like everything else) compares the price against its trigger — floor(min(W × 0.8, W − O − 65,536)) for window W and output cap O. This session is young, so nothing happens; in a long session the oldest balanced span would be replaced by one LLM-written summary in <compacted-summary> tags, keeping the newest 16% of W − O verbatim.
steps.representation:
W = model window, O = output cap
trigger = floor(min(W x 0.8, W - O - 65,536))
pending request priced via ctx.tokenMeter
under trigger -> no compaction this step
steps.title: Price the context

modules.label: agent.ts:688 — deriveMessages() at the step boundary

steps.narrative: The loop holds no mutable conversation state. At the step boundary it calls session.deriveMessages() and folds the append-only log — system prompt, user events, assistant events, tool results — into the message history for this one request. This is the project's stated invariant in action: model-visible ⟺ logged. Anything that should reach the model must first become a session event.
steps.representation:
deriveMessages(log) ->
  system prompt (preset persona + project instructions)
  + folded user / assistant / tool events
  = the entire model-visible history
# no side channel: if it is not logged, the model cannot see it
steps.title: Derive the context from the log

steps.narrative: prepareCall builds the request through the ctx.llm seam — the loop never talks to a provider directly. In the Standard preset's native presentation, every tool mounted in this agent's scope contributes its full schema to the request: bash, read, write, edit, grep, glob, the job and schedule and goal tools, and the rest of the generated catalog. There is no tool search and no deferred loading; which tools exist at all was decided at composition time, by the preset's plugin rows.
steps.representation:
request via ctx.llm (official DeepSeek API)
  messages: derived history
  tools: [ bash, read, write, edit, grep, glob, ... ]
         every mounted schema — no tool search
  + dsh_session_log: events since watermark (step 8)
steps.title: Build the request: every tool, natively

steps.narrative: kick() is running its while (await this.turn()) {} loop — no step budget, no turn budget. The streamed response settles into the log as assistant/message and assistant/attempt events, and the model's first calls are reads: read the settings page, grep for the theme handling. Read-only effects need no approval under the ask policy, so they execute straight away (at most 10 calls in parallel per step), and their results are appended to the log for the next step to re-derive.
steps.representation:
stream -> assistant/message, assistant/attempt events
tool calls: read(settings page), grep("theme")
  read-only effects -> no approval under ask
results appended to the log; next step re-derives
steps.title: The model reads first

steps.narrative: Now the model calls edit — a write. Under the ask policy, the tools/pre-execute waterfall demands a decision, dispatched as an approval/request to the composed answerers; the Web UI asks, and the user approves. The approval covers exactly this one call — there is no always-allow. Both the request and the decision are written to the log (approval/asked, approval/decided), but neither is model-visible: the model will see only the edit's outcome. Had the answerer been missing, thrown, or answered off-vocabulary, the result would be unavailable — and the call blocked.
steps.representation:
approval/asked    { tool: edit, one-shot request }  -> log only
Web UI answerer -> approve
approval/decided  { outcome: approved }             -> log only
# the model sees neither event — only the tool result
steps.title: The edit asks

steps.narrative: The edit lands through the in-process filesystem fence: the per-call sandbox mode is workspace-write, and the observation policy's read-before-edit and version guards are satisfied by step 5's reads. The model then verifies with bash — the typecheck runs under the OS sandbox (bubblewrap first on Linux, Landlock as the fallback rung), wrapped by the timeout-policy guard at the bash tool's 60-second default. Enforcement completeness is reported per call; had no backend been able to enforce the mode, the call would have failed with SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE rather than running unconfined.
steps.representation:
edit -> fs fence: workspace-write, read-before-edit ok
bash("npm run typecheck")
  -> bubblewrap (fallback: Landlock)
  -> timeout-policy guard: 60 s budget
  result + enforcement reported: full
steps.title: Execute under the sandbox

steps.narrative: The typecheck passes. The model replies with a summary and no tool calls, so the step returns completed; the loop dispatches the serial agent/turn-stopping hook — the one built-in veto point over turn end — no composed plugin objects, and the turn ends. One thing rode along with every request this turn: because the provider is the official DeepSeek API, each carried a dsh_session_log field with the canonical session events since the last server-accepted watermark (at most 8 MiB, at-least-once). The upload plugin is mounted in the base bundle and enabled by default; a Settings switch pauses it, but the backlog is not purged.
steps.representation:
final step: reply with no tool calls -> completed
agent/turn-stopping dispatched — no veto — turn ends
every official-API request this turn carried:
  dsh_session_log: [events since watermark, <= 8 MiB]
server accepts -> delivery-accepted event advances it
steps.title: Finish — and the log leaves
